as_read: Conflicting with no clear benefit: small positive trials with poor reporting and no named primary outcome, a funded 12-week trial with no between-group difference in adiposity, and reviews that call the effect unproven or limited by poor quality.

quote.text: Overall efficacy of Irvingia gabonensis seed extract supplementation on weight loss seems positive but is limited due to poor methodological quality and the insufficient reporting of the clinical trials.

proposed_decision_text: Eight labels print African mango seed extract 1,200 mg and one prints Irvingia gabonensis IGOB 131 at 150 mg, with no weight claim in the rows. No study read meets rule 2. The stored trial tested IGOB131 150 mg twice daily for 10 weeks in 102 overweight or obese volunteers and reported improved body weight and metabolic markers against placebo, but neither its abstract nor the text passages searched in its open full text names a primary outcome, and part of its funds and the extract came from the manufacturer (19254366). A 12-week trial of 300 mg/day kernel extract found no between-group difference in metabolism, inflammation or aerobic capacity, with benefit limited to plasma vitamin C and adiponectin, and it names no primary outcome (36364907). A 90-day trial of 150 mg twice daily in 24 patients with metabolic syndrome reports within-group changes and remission in 58.3% versus 16.7%, with no primary outcome named (29336718). A one-month trial used 1.05 g of seeds three times a day, a food-like amount of a preparation these labels do not print, with no primary outcome named (15916709). A meta-analysis of five trials reports weight loss but rates four as high risk of bias and says the one low-risk trial had no significantly different outcomes, and it gives no dose in its abstract (31855111). A 2013 systematic review calls the effect unproven (23419021), a 2020 review of herbal medicines finds insufficient evidence to recommend them (31984610), and a network meta-analysis ranks African mango first while asking for higher quality studies, on mostly indirect comparisons (40420357). 1,200 mg is above every extract dose tested in these trials. Abstracts, plus full text passages for 19254366 and 36364907.
stop_list: The label's IGOB 131 row states the material; the eight 1,200 mg rows print seed extract with no standardization.
clinician_items: 23419021: adverse events in the included trials were headache and sleep difficulty.
36364907: full text reports side effects of nausea (6 cases), constipation (1) and thirst (1), described as not severe.
stored_rating_note: Stored positive_moderate rests on 19254366 alone. The stored outcome's -12.8 kg versus -0.7 kg is not in the abstract; tables in the full text were not checked. The stored sample of 102 is completers; the full text says 120 were randomized. positive_moderate looks high given 31855111 and 36364907.
unread_notes: 19254366 (PMC2651880) and 36364907 (PMC9656030) were opened in full text and searched for primary outcome, funding, dose and completion, not read end to end; the tool reads paragraph text, so tables were not seen. 36364907 sized its sample on fat oxidation rate but does not call it primary in the passages read. 36364907 is sponsored by Blackmores Limited, which also supplied the tablets. All others abstracts only; 29336718 and 31855111 have no PMC id. One search used (13 hits). Hits seen and not read: 18377661 (combination), 36816319, 31793087, 23777875, 20847896 (reviews).
